conventions.convention: State spaces are finite and nonempty; all raw weights are strictly positive and finite. The directed divergence is χ²(ν∥μ)=Σx μ(x)(ν(x)/μ(x)−1)².
Bridge stages have indices 0≤k<K, K≥1, and positive integer sample counts. All supplied draws across all stages are mutually independent and have their specified exact stage laws.
Partition sums define the sampling laws and target ratios but are not numerical inputs to the raw-weight estimators.

Rational weight and observable intervals are certified input premises. They are converted outward to finite dyadic intervals; the algorithm does not derive weight bounds from energies or evaluate exponentials.

An expectation enclosure is returned only when the partition interval has strictly positive lower endpoint and the quotient operation is finite. Overflow and other unresolved branches carry no normalized-expectation enclosure claim.

The product-law example assumes distinct strictly positive probability mass functions, m,N≥1, and a fixed tolerance ε>0. Its exponential sample-size requirement concerns only the specified one-stage estimator.

load_bearing.statement: For finite nonempty X, finite strictly positive weights w0,w1, and n≥1 independent draws with common law π0=w0/Z0, the raw-ratio sample mean has expectation Z1/Z0 and relative variance χ²(π1∥π0)/n.

Given an enumerated finite nonempty state space, positive exact weights, a real observable, certified rational input intervals and a finite dyadic format, convert endpoints outward, form outward-rounded partition and weighted sums, and return their finite intervals or an unresolved status. Return the outward expectation quotient only with a strictly positive denominator lower endpoint.

For K≥1 adjacent pairs of finite positive weights and supplied mutually independent exact stage samples, compute each adjacent raw-ratio sample mean and return their product; no partition sum is required as a numerical input.

published_dependencies.used_for: The formal normalized weighted variable in the partition-ratio proof. Its known-normalizer requirement is explicitly preserved rather than imposed on the raw-ratio computation.
The finite-sample variance-of-an-average identity. Finite positive weights ensure full support and finite second moment; the AC-dependent CLT conclusion is unused.
Finite dyadic formats, directed conversion of rational endpoints, and explicit overflow handling.
Finite dyadic real intervals and finite expression DAGs with shared exact intermediate values.
Outward-rounded addition, multiplication and division with denominator-domain and overflow restrictions.
Containment after finite endpoint conversion and the separation of overflow from finite enclosure claims.
Enclosure propagation through the finite partition, weighted-sum and quotient DAGs, including shared nodes.
